title: Learning to Swim at Forty
summary: Nadia was always afraid of water. On her fortieth birthday, she decided it was time to change that.
paragraphs: Nadia had never learned to swim. When she was a child, her family lived far from the sea, and there was no swimming pool in her small town. Once, when she was seven, she fell into a river while playing with her cousins. Her uncle pulled her out quickly, but from that day she was afraid of deep water.

For more than thirty years, Nadia found ways to avoid swimming. On family holidays, she sat on the beach with a book while her husband and children played in the waves. When friends invited her to the pool, she always had an excuse. She told herself it did not matter. But secretly she felt sad every time she watched the others having fun.

On her fortieth birthday, her daughter Leila gave her a small card. Inside was a ticket for ten swimming lessons for adults. “You always tell me I can do anything if I try,” Leila wrote. “Now it's your turn.”

Nadia almost cried. She wanted to say no, but she could not refuse her daughter's gift. The following Monday evening, she stood at the edge of the pool, shaking. There were five other people in the class, all adults who could not swim. Their teacher, a calm young man called Tom, smiled at them. “Today we are not going to swim,” he said. “Today we are just going to make friends with the water.”

For the first lesson, they only walked in the shallow end and put their faces in the water. Nadia's heart was beating fast, but nothing bad happened. In the second lesson, they learned to float on their backs while Tom held them. By the fifth lesson, Nadia could kick across the pool holding a board.

Not every lesson went well. One evening she swallowed a lot of water and wanted to give up. But the other students encouraged her. “We are all scared,” said an older man called Ben. “We are scared together.” They laughed, and Nadia got back in the water.

At the last lesson, Tom asked each student to swim one length of the pool without help. When it was Nadia's turn, she took a deep breath and pushed off from the wall. Her arms were tired and her style was not beautiful, but she reached the other side. Everyone clapped. Leila, who was watching from the seats, was cheering louder than anyone.
That summer, on the family holiday, Nadia did not sit on the beach with her book. She swam in the sea with her children, and it was the best holiday of her life.

questions.question: Why was Nadia afraid of deep water?
options: She saw an accident on television
She fell into a river as a child
Her parents told her it was dangerous
She was attacked by a fish
questions.explanation: When she was seven she fell into a river, and from that day she was afraid of deep water.

questions.question: What did Nadia usually do on beach holidays?
options: She sat on the beach and read
questions.explanation: She sat on the beach with a book while the others played in the waves.

questions.question: What did the class do in the first lesson?
options: They walked in shallow water and put their faces in
questions.explanation: They only walked in the shallow end and put their faces in the water.

questions.question: What helped Nadia when she wanted to give up?
options: Tom gave her a free lesson
She changed to a different pool
questions.explanation: The other students encouraged her, and Ben said they were all scared together.

questions.question: Which word best describes Nadia at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: She overcame her fear, swam a full length and enjoyed swimming with her children.

grammar.structure: Past perfect with never (had never + past participle)
grammar.explanation: Had never + past participle says something did not happen at any time before a point in the past.
grammar.example: Nadia had never learned to swim.

exercise.question: Choose the correct option: Before that holiday, she ___ in the sea.
exercise.explanation: We talk about the time before a past moment (that holiday), so we use had never swum.

grammar.explanation: We use am/is/are going to + verb for plans and intentions.
grammar.example: Today we are not going to swim.

exercise.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Next week we going to practise floating.
Next week we are going practise floating.
Next week we are going to practise floating.
Next week we go to practising floating.
exercise.explanation: The form is am/is/are + going to + verb.
